The hook does not distinguish between (a) the codex command attempting to mutate git and (b) a prompt body whose text references git-mutation verbs. The hook block is a false positive in this case but cannot be bypassed (per ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md § Subagent Hook Discipline — wrapping the codex command in a script file or substituting verbs to evade the hook is forbidden).

key_findings: Q1 PASS_WITH_CAVEAT: { ... || true; } pattern is directionally correct under set -euo pipefail; brace groups normalize grep's exit 1 to 0; pipeline status equals wc -l's status. Caveat: || true also masks grep exit 2 (regex-compile error or missing/unreadable file). Mitigation: add [ -r "$file" ] precheck to catch unreadable file with explicit return 2. Documented as L14b for residual regex-compile masking.
Q2 PASS: L15/L16/L17 are all real uncovered deploy branches; deploy-side recovery snapshot failure (L16) is genuinely NOT covered by rollback's S14.

Q3 EXPANDED: codex flagged 3 adjacent gaps — (a) L17 should split into y-path AND n-path (deploy.sh:335-340 n-path uncovered); (b) L18 candidate: deploy.sh:318-320 missing-daemon.state.json branch (no scenario invokes M-DAEMONMOCK.3's omit_daemon for deploy); (c) L2 under-characterized — deploy.sh:130-136 untracked-files confirm gate has both y/n paths uncovered, S05 only covers tracked-dirty exit 1. Plus a test-design pitfall: S03b's fixture must make dev-SHA locally known but not on fork/* — otherwise deploy aborts earlier at line 146-147.
Q4 CONCUR: S17.10 + S17.11 not over-testing — bug is exit-code behavior under pipefail, explicit exit-code coverage is justified.

Q5 CONCUR: S17.10 covers cases A+B (matches all filtered), S17.11 covers case C (zero raw matches), existing S17.8 covers case D (bare violation), S17.9 covers raw count negative control. Sufficient if assertions check both count AND helper exit status.
